atoms.b: Women in Anglo-Saxon Britain had much less freedom than women in ((++Britain space)) today.
Women were expected to ((++marry divorce)) and have children at around 15 years old, which was very ((++risky easy)) due to poor childbirth care.
While men did physical tasks, such as ((++farming resting)) and going to battle, women took care of the ((++children invaders)) and the household.

Fill in the gaps in this conversation between an Anglo-Saxon chief and his daughter.

atoms.b: Ebba, guess what! I have ((++arranged stolen)) a marriage between you and Algar from the neighbouring tribe. You will be a peace-weaver!

hint.text: Peace-weavers were women of high status who entered arranged marriages to create lasting peace between tribes
hint.label: Peace-weaver

atoms.b: I’m not sure about ((++marrying carrying)) Algar. Everybody says he is unpleasant, and I don’t want to live with the neighbouring tribe.
Are you sure? You would bring peace to our tribes through the bond of ((++family friendship)).
I absolutely refuse. Algar would be a ((++horrible lovely)) person to marry.
Very well. The final decision is ((++yours mine)).

feedback.end: The woman involved was always able to refuse the marriage if she wished.

atoms.text: Although noblewomen also had limited freedom, some still managed to gain significant power.
Aethelfleda, the daughter of King Alfred the Great, became the ruler of a kingdom and fought against invaders when her husband died.
atoms.sound: Ethelfledda, the daughter of King Alfred the Great, became the ruler of a kingdom and fought against invaders when her husband died.

atoms.a: What two things do you think helped Aethelfleda gain power?
atoms.sound: What two things do you think helped Ethelfledda gain power?
b: ++She was the daughter of a king.
++Her husband’s death gave her the chance to rule on her own.

feedback.finish: Some women joined the Church as an alternative to marriage. Nuns spent their time praying and worshipping.

instruction.text: What two things do you think nuns were not allowed to do?

atoms.b: Hilda of Whitby was a nun living in the north of England in the ((++7th 21st)) century.
She was so wise that kings from all over Britain travelled to ((++seek ignore)) her advice.

finish.text: Hilda of Whitby and Aethelfleda were rare examples of women gaining power. The vast majority of women in Anglo-Saxon Britain looked after the home and children.
finish.sound: Hilda of Whitby and Ethelfledda were rare examples of women gaining power. The vast majority of women in Anglo-Saxon Britain looked after the home and children.
